draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Bhimashankar! The black stone Shiva temple a minute away holds one of the 12 Jyotirlingas, and it dates back to the 13th century. The Bhima River starts right here in this village too.
draft.hungryLine: My notes don't name any eateries here, so if you're trekking up, pack your snacks and plenty of water.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Bhimashankar Temple is a 1 min walk, Rokda Hanuman Mandir is 14 min, and the Nagphani viewpoint is 18 min away.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Walk out to the Nagphani viewpoint, 18 min from here, and take in the forest range around you.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The temple's central hall and dome were improved in the 18th century by Nana Phadnavis.

spots.name: Bhimashankar Temple
spots.detail: 1 min walk · Black stone temple with one of Maharashtra's three Jyotirlingas

spots.name: Nagphani
spots.detail: 18 min walk · A viewpoint over the hills

spots.name: Bhimshankar Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.detail: All around the temple · Semi-evergreen forest spread over Pune, Raigad and Thane

legends.title: In the saints' footsteps
legends.body: The medieval saint Namdev wrote that Saint Jnaneshwar travelled to Tryambakeshwar and then on to Bhimashankar. Namdev came here himself too.

legends.title: Gods in the rock
legends.body: On the hills of Manmad village nearby, there are old rock carvings of the God Bhimashankar, Bhootings and Amba-Ambika.

tips.title: Carry three litres of water.
tips.body: Outside the monsoon, the trek has long stretches under the sun and dehydration is a real risk.

tips.title: Dress for the temple.
tips.body: This is one of the holiest pilgrimage spots in India, so cover up when you visit the shrine.

story.title: Black stone shrine
story.body: Writings mention the Bhimashankaram shrine and the Bhimarathi river as far back as the 13th century. The temple itself is carved in black stone.

story.title: Saints on the road
story.body: Saint Namdev recorded that Jnaneshwar visited Bhimashankar after Tryambakeshwar. Namdev made the trip as well.

story.title: Nana Phadnavis builds
story.body: In the 18th century, Nana Phadnavis improved the sabhamandap, the central hall, and the shikhara, the dome.

story.title: A protected forest
story.body: The forest around the temple became a wildlife sanctuary in 1974. It sits between 2100 and 3800 feet and covers parts of three districts.

story.title: Pilgrims and trekkers
story.body: Bhimashankar is a key pilgrimage centre and a popular trek, about 100 km from Pune. The forest here still holds rare plants and animals.
